teaching_structure.teaching_activities:
Start with a simple song about family (e.g., "Finger Family Song") to engage students and introduce the theme.
Ask students: "Who is in your family?" and "What do you like to do with your family?"
teaching_structure.learning_activities:
Share names of family members and activities they do together.
Listen attentively to the teacher's introduction.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Dictated words are written correctly

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Introduce a simple story titled "My Wonderful Family" (a short, teacher-created story about a family's daily activities, e.g., eating breakfast, playing, reading together).
teaching_structure.learning_activities:
Explain what "dictation" means (listening carefully and writing down words).
Remind students of CVC (Consonant-Vowel-Consonant) word structure.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Dictated words are written correctly

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explain the activity: "Today, you will draw a picture of your family. Next to your drawing, you will choose one of the words we dictated and write a short sentence using that word to describe your family or an activity you do together."
teaching_structure.learning_activities:
Write a simple sentence using the chosen word, relating it to their family drawing.
Share their drawings and sentences with a partner or the class (optional, time permitting).
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Dictated words are written correctly

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Use portfolios, performance assessment, and questions and answers
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students present portfolio, answer questions orally and perform tasks
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Dictated words are written correctly

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Introduce the concept of personal pronouns as words that take the place of nouns (like names). Explain that today's focus will be on 'I' (referring to oneself) and 'You' (referring to the person being spoken to).

Listen to the introduction of personal pronouns 'I' and 'You'.
